Subject: Redwood order form (draft) — invoicing entity & min-commit amortization

Hi Sarah / procurement team,

Thanks again for the productive call yesterday. Attached is our working redline of the Order Form and the commercial appendix (Pegasus_OrderForm_v1_redlines.pdf). Two quick items we want to surface before legal runs a full pass:

1) Invoicing entity: Pegasus indicated they prefer invoices to go to the US parent (Pegasus Bio, Inc.) but the PO will be issued by the UK subsidiary. We need to confirm which legal entity will accept liability and whether Pegasus can provide a VAT registration certificate. If invoices go to the US entity, our billing ops will require an explicit remit-to direction and VAT handling note.

2) Minimum commit amortization: highlighted Section 2.2 — Pegasus wants the full annual commit to be payable up front but amortized for accounting purposes. We can accept upfront payment with an invoice schedule that shows the upfront charge and monthly recognition, but legal/finance needs to align on the invoice flow and refund/clawback language if usage materially exceeds forecasts.

I copied Ben and Karthik for pricing/ops and contract redline coordination. Can you confirm whether procurement will: (a) provide a sample PO and remit-to entity; (b) share a VAT certificate? If you prefer, we can stage the order form so the billing entity is gated behind procurement evidence.

Next steps we propose: Redwood to send the annotated OF -> Pegasus to confirm remit/PO -> Redwood legal to do final pass on MSA/OF redlines (we'd like legal turnaround of 3 business days if possible).

Thanks — Marissa

Marissa — quick notes from pricing/ops after I reviewed Sarah's reply and the VAT cert:

- Invoicing to UK entity is OK, but we need a small appendix in the OF that maps invoice recipient -> accounting entity -> tax handling (we already do this in other multi-entity deals). I can draft the appendix.

- On upfront invoice: ops can send a single invoice for 100% at signing to the UK remit-to, with a PDF schedule attached that shows monthly recognition. That satisfies their accounting; the only blocker is refund/clawback language. We should add a clause that usage above X% of forecast triggers a true-up invoice within 30 days.

- Net terms: Pegasus asked for Net45 in our call. For this ARR/commit size we prefer Net30 but can be flexible to Net45 for a small premium/contract credit. Recommend we offer Net45 if they take a 2% prepay discount or allow us to keep the upfront as non-refundable against usage. Thoughts?

Ben

Kimberly — can you weigh in on the redline risk around the upfront non-refundable language and the clawback timeframe? Also, tax evidence was attached; can you confirm if the VAT cert is sufficient or if finance needs additional residency docs? If not, we should request a brief letter from their tax counsel.

I pasted my recommended quick playbook below to close this without a long legal loop: 

- Option A (preferred): Accept UK invoicing to Pegasus Bio UK Ltd. Redwood issues one upfront invoice (100%) to the remit-to in the UK. Invoice includes a monthly recognition schedule. Net terms: Net45 with no discount. Add a usage true-up clause: if actual usage > 140% of forecast in a 90-day window, Pegasus will owe a true-up invoice for the overage billed within 30 days. No refunds for under-usage for prepay.

- Option B (compromise): Net30 + 2% prepay discount and allow partial refund subject to 60-day notice and capped at 20% of commit amount.

Please advise legal risk and suggest edits to the OF redline. I can present these options to Pegasus on Friday.

Thanks — Marissa

Marissa / team — read through the redlines and Sarah's VAT attestation. Quick take:

- VAT evidence: The certificate looks valid but ops needs the registration number in a standardized format; ask them to confirm registration ID and effective date. If Pegasus invoices to the UK legal entity, VAT treatment is straightforward. If they later request US invoicing, we'll need a residency statement and potentially a W-8/W-9 depending on remit.

- Upfront non-refundable language: acceptable if we limit the no-refund carve to 12 months and include a mutual audit clause. We should avoid hard non-refundable language >12 months. Also recommend adding a cap to early termination refunds tied to used credits, not the full prepay.

- Clawback/true-up: 30 days is tight for their larger customers; suggest 45 days for reconciliation (we can still push for 30 but expect negotiation).

I'll redline the specific language in the attached PDF and return the OF with edits. Karthik/Ben, I'll align on netterms premium language; Ben, please confirm the margin impact if we move to Net45 without a discount.

Kimberly Park
Head of Finance Operations | Redwood Inference

Sarah — thanks for the VAT cert and quick replies. Attached is the OF with Redwood legal + ops suggested edits (Pegasus_OrderForm_v1_redlines.pdf). Summary of agreed path we propose to present to procurement/legalops: 

1) Invoicing & remit: Redwood will invoice Pegasus Bio UK Ltd (PO to be issued by Pegasus UK). Please confirm the exact remit-to name and VAT reg ID to populate the invoice appendix.

2) Upfront payment & amortization: Pegasus to pay 100% at signing to the UK remit-to. Redwood will include a monthly recognition schedule in the invoice PDF for their internal accounting. Prepay will be non-refundable with a capped early termination refund (12 months pro-rata of used credits).

3) Net terms: Redwood proposes Net45 for this deal without a prepay discount. If procurement prefers Net30, Redwood can offer a 2% prepay discount instead.

4) True-up: If usage exceeds 140% of forecast within a 90-day lookback, Pegasus will be invoiced for overages and will have 45 days to pay.

Next steps: If that path looks OK, please (a) confirm remit-to name + VAT reg ID; (b) return a sample PO; and (c) confirm DocuSign contact so we can send the order form for signature. I've also included a DocuSign link to the draft order form for their legal ops review: https://app.docusign.com/OrderForm/RGW-2389

If procurement wants to negotiate Option B (Net30 + 2% discount), let me know and we'll route back to Ben.

Best — Marissa
